summary.intent: Participate as 'claude-code' agent in a multi-agent RFD authoring session to review and refine a memory/experiences design document for an agent memory system, converging toward a shippable RFD.
summary.outcome: The RFD was substantially revised: Option A (SQLite-based local cache) was committed as the chosen substrate, `source_signal` semantics were pinned as a structured slug, a migration path from the existing `.entire/memory-loop.json` JSON store was added, and the server-side RFD was made an explicit hard prerequisite. Stance was 'request-changes' due to the unresolvable server-side dependency.

repo: Live user-promoted memory records exist at `.entire/memory-loop.json` with structured fields like `repo_rule-checkpoint-repo-go-git-test-packages-need-configloader-plugin`; any migration must preserve these.

Two overlapping design docs existed with the same date prefix (2026-04-16-agent-memory-design.md and 2026-04-16-agent-memory-lessons-experiences-design.md) — the RFD did not acknowledge the parallel document.
The memory system uses a SQLite-backed insightsdb cache (cache.go) alongside a JSON memory-loop store — these are distinct layers.
The codebase separates memoryloop (generator.go, memoryloop.go) from insightsdb cache logic.

code.finding: Core memory loop implementation; reviewed to understand existing memory storage patterns before editing the RFD.
Memory generation logic; reviewed to understand how memories are produced and stored.
SQLite-backed analysis cache; the RFD's proposed new substrate; reviewed to understand existing schema patterns.
API client reviewed to understand what server-side endpoints exist (or are missing) for the memory sync protocol.
Live JSON store with user-promoted memory records; migration path to SQLite must not drop these records.

workflow: In multi-agent RFD sessions, the first agent sets the tone by investigating the codebase before forming opinions rather than just editing text.
When an RFD presents multiple options without committing to one, the reviewing agent should make the decision and reframe the alternatives as historical/informative rather than re-litigating them.
Option-specific schema columns (like `graph_neighborhood_json` for Option B) should not leak into supposedly option-agnostic shared schemas.
Explicit server-side API contract minimums (which endpoints must exist before a given PR) should be stated in the RFD rather than hand-waved as a parallel dependency.

friction: The RFD kept re-litigating Option A vs B across multiple sections (§5, §7, §12, §13, §15), requiring many targeted edits to converge the framing.
`source_signal` was used with two different semantics in the same doc (prototype embedding input vs. outcome comparison field), requiring explicit clarification.
The server-side RFD dependency could not be resolved from the client side — left as an open concern.
Multiple rounds of read-then-edit were needed to verify section coherence after each structural change.
open_items: Server-side RFD must be authored and approved before PR 1 / PR 9 of the implementation plan can proceed.
A few smaller open questions remained for subsequent agents to address (not enumerated in transcript).
The parallel `2026-04-16-agent-memory-design.md` doc's relationship to this RFD was flagged but not fully resolved.
